justification: Progressive amplitude hardening is local in E06/E09; communication may enter only through balance.
Hookean and neo-Hookean branches support waves without a finite extension barrier.
Recovery follows a conservative single-well energy; the label is sufficient in the elastic sector, not logically necessary for dissipative asymptotic recovery.
Gradient and integral nonlocal operators have related long-wave expansions but are not exactly equivalent at finite wavelength.
Exponential/polynomial hardening lacks a finite endpoint; a poorly chosen one-invariant barrier need not harden every tensor path.
Coercivity acts at infinity; finite extensibility acts at a finite domain boundary.
Conservative hyperelastic systems propagate waves without dissipation; dissipative systems may overdamp them.
